newsitem.title: UK: Britain to host Nazi gold conference in December.
newsitem.headline: Britain to host Nazi gold conference in December.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it would host an international conference in December to resolve problems posed by millions of dollars of gold seized by the Nazis in World War Two.
Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said the conference would look into the question of compensation for individual victims of Nazi persecution.
The conference was also intended to pool available knowledge on historical facts relating to gold looted by the Nazis from countries and individuals.
The conference, expected to attract delegates from 25 countries, will be held in London on December 2-4.
"The government shares the concern of the international community about the origins and disposal of Nazi gold," Cook said in a statment.
"I hope that the London conference will pool international knowledge and reach conclusions on this important issue."
Cook pledged to hold an international conference on Nazi gold soon after he became Foreign Secretary last May, when the Labour Party won a landslide election victory.
The conference is being held under the auspices of the Tripartite Gold Commission, set up in 1946 and run by Britain, the United States and France to restore looted gold to its rightful owners.
The Tripartite Commission has always maintained that all of the gold it is holding was looted from the central banks of countries occupied by the Nazis.
But Jewish groups have maintained that between five and 10 percent of the gold belonged to private individuals.
Lord Janner, a prominent member of Britain's Jewish community and chairman of the Holocaust Educational Trust, welcomed Cook's "powerful initiative".
"This conference will give new impetus to the vital campaign for truth and justice on Nazi gold," Janner said.
The Foreign Office said there had been claims that the Tripartite Commission monetary gold pool also contained gold stolen from individuals.

Foreign Office research had shown that every effort was made to keep separate monetary gold from individuals' gold. But some gold from individuals, resmelted into monetary form by the Nazis, may have found its way into the Tripartite Commission pool.
The Foreign Office said it believed that the results of the research would strengthen the case for examining the issue in more detail and for looking at ways to compensate needy victims of Nazism.
The Tripartite Gold Commission has distributed about four billion dollars worth of gold to central banks. None has gone to individuals.
It still has about 68 million dollars left in its coffers. Several countries have claims on the remaining gold and would have to be part of any decision.
